summary: This work shows that rotation errors and phase errors in weakly anharmonic qubits follow from a single parametrization $\mathcal{X}(\pi/2) = Z(\delta)X(\pi/2+\epsilon)Z(\delta)$, enabling DRAPE, a single Ramsey-type protocol that simultaneously calibrates both errors by identifying a crossing point in phase-correction sweeps. DRAPE achieves Heisenberg scaling for phase estimation while saturating the standard quantum limit for rotation errors, demonstrated on an IBM transmon with $|1\rangle\leftrightarrow|2\rangle$ encoding, reducing over-rotation from $0.997°$ to $-0.007°$ and phase error from $2.52°$ to $0.0052°$ per gate.
motivation: Coherent control errors in superconducting qubits take two generic forms—over/under-rotation and phase errors—whose suppression ordinarily requires iterated calibration loops between separate amplified-error protocols (APE and ARE), making scalable error characterization inefficient as qubit counts grow.
method: By analyzing the driven dynamics of weakly anharmonic qubits through Schrieffer-Wolff transformation and the toggling frame, the authors derive that rotation error $\epsilon$ depends only on drive amplitude while phase error $\delta$ depends on $\epsilon$ via the ac Stark shift, exposing a one-directional interplay. DRAPE sweeps a DRAG correction coefficient $\beta$ during a composite Ramsey sequence with $k$ pseudo-identity pairs; a crossing point in the measured population versus $\beta$ simultaneously reveals both corrections without iteration.
result: On the $|1\rangle\leftrightarrow|2\rangle$ transition of an IBM transmon with anharmonicity $|\Delta_2|/2\pi = 307$ MHz and drive amplitude $\Omega_0/2\pi = 40$ MHz, DRAPE extracted $\epsilon = (0.997\pm0.395)°$ and $\beta_0 = -0.3894\pm0.0002$, reducing coherent errors by two to three orders of magnitude—validated independently by APE and ARE protocols without requiring calibration loops.
